title: A priced model without a conflict next to unpriced models with one, one of them all disputed
matrix: input, output, cache-read and cache-write breakdowns
policy: P9 (#58 re-review of 5f48f65): a model without a price keeps its disputed tokens disputed, counted once (unknown + disputed = its total), so any total holding them is provisional, never a lower bound. Its own cost is unavailable (n/a), and it stays named as unpriced even when every token is disputed. The cost strings are checked in QuantityTests.unpricedConflictStaysProvisional.
derivation: a Haiku 4.5, 30 = 10+20: [1, 1, 5m 10, 1h 20], exact: 1 + 5 + 12.5 + 40 = 58.5 micro-dollars, complete. b claude-test-1 (no price), flat 100 vs 200+100: [1, 1], 100 unresolved, 200 disputed = 302 tokens: 102 unknown + 200 disputed, no minimum without a price, unavailable. Step 1: 32 + 302 = 334, 200 disputed, partial. Step 2 adds c claude-test-2 (no price), flat 0 vs 50+30: [0, 0], 80 disputed: 0 unknown + 80 disputed, unavailable. 414 tokens, 280 disputed. The known cost stays 58.5 micro-dollars throughout. Before this fix the unpriced models' disputed tokens were counted as unknown only, so the total read as a lower bound (>=).
